newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss machine industry says Jan-Sept orders fall.
newsitem.headline: Swiss machine industry says Jan-Sept orders fall.

text.p: Swiss engineering and machinery companies, which account for about 45 percent of Swiss exports, said new orders fell 7.8 percent in the first nine months of 1996 due to a European economic slump and a strong Swiss franc.
The Association of Swiss Machine Makers (ASM/VSM) said a recovery in orders was possible in 1997 if major markets in Western Europe and Japan recover, as widely predicted.
The industry also expected a positive effect from a weakening in the Swiss franc since September, partly due to a gradual loosening of money supply by the Swiss National Bank.
"In this respect, the ASM hopes the central bank will continue to ease monetary policy, which has had a positive effect so far," the association said in a statement.
It said the 7.8-percent drop in total orders compared with growth of 4.8 percent in the first nine months of last year.
Orders from abroad slipped for the first time in five years, down by 7.7 percent against growth of 9.5 percent in the same period last year.
Domestic orders dropped 8.1 percent, a larger decline than a slump of 3.1 percent a year ago.
Sales declined by 5.2 percent among the 180 ASM members surveyed for the study, the association said.
Exports rose by a nominal 3.1 percent in the nine month period, reflecting the good influx of orders last year.

"Exports to European Union countries increased only slightly, but growth rates in Asia were once again pleasing (Singapore +34 percent, Indonesia +26 percent, India +17 percent and Japan +14 percent)," the ASM said.
Exports to the United States grew by 4.1 percent.
